target: General SWE / backend software engineering internships (big tech + strong startups), 2026-27 cycle

bullet_feedback.bullet: Co-founded a 110+ member student product studio that has shipped 5 live products, and personally built Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries for one, Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days
bullet_feedback.problem: Two different ownership levels are fused: '110+ member' and '5 live products' are the studio's output, '20,000+ visits' is the product's adoption, and the only personal contribution ('personally built Redis caching') has no stated effect. The biggest number on the bullet does not measure the candidate's work.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I am trying to separate what this person did from what the team did. As written, a skeptical reader credits the caching with nothing and discounts the 20,000+ as borrowed adoption; a generous one over-credits and then gets surprised in the interview.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the Redis cache changed for Tortuga (load time, DB load, cost, stability during the traffic spike), and what the candidate did as co-founder beyond caching (e.g., technical lead on which products).
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Split the founder/studio claim from the engineering claim, or state the reason the cache was needed (the traffic it absorbed) so the 20,000+ visits explain the engineering instead of decorating it.

bullet_feedback.bullet: For a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR, built a Python pipeline that renders AnyGrasp’s candidate grasps on multi-camera images as Open3D overlays for a vision-language model, and tuned its prompts so it picks right more often
bullet_feedback.problem: The outcome 'picks right more often' is vague and informal; 'tuned its prompts' is the weakest part of the bullet and it ends on it. 'aimed at ICLR' leaves submission status unclear.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Every other role states a concrete result; this one ends on an unmeasured improvement, which reads as 'prompt tweaking' and undercuts the more interesting engineering (rendering 3D grasp candidates as multi-view overlays for a VLM).
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: how 'right' was judged (grasp success, agreement with ground truth) and roughly how much it improved, if known; clarify whether the paper is submitted, in prep, or targeted.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the pipeline's purpose in plain words (letting a VLM choose among robot grasp candidates by seeing them drawn on camera images), and either state the measured improvement or cut 'and tuned its prompts...' rather than end on a vague claim.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: 'strict access limits' is ambiguous (rate limits? permissions? query quotas?), and the bullet opens with the constraint so the action is buried until the second clause. 'to cut database queries' is intent, not a result.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The design decision (precompute a category index + cache because the source table is constrained) is the most interviewable backend idea at Capital One, but a reader has to re-parse the sentence to find it and can't tell what the constraint actually was.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what kind of access limit (rate limit, read permission scope, query budget).
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the action ('Precomputed popular workflows into a category tree...') and move the constraint into a short 'because' clause after; name the limit type in plain words.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting one large Claude skill into smaller sub-skills that call Python tools for search and validation, after CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs showed where time went
bullet_feedback.problem: 'AI workflow generation' and 'Claude skill' are undefined for a reader outside the team: it is not clear what a workflow is, who generates it, or that a 'skill' is an LLM agent component.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The method (profiling, then decomposition into tool-calling sub-steps) is good, but a non-LLM hiring manager can't tell what system got faster or who waited on it, so the 65% floats without context.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: who uses the generated workflows (developers creating test data, per the third bullet?) and what a 'workflow' is in one or two words.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add a short noun phrase that says what is being generated and for whom (e.g., 'test-data workflows for developers'), reusing the context the third bullet already gives.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo’s public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate
bullet_feedback.problem: 'space-topic research tool' does not say what the tool does, and 'Deployed' undersells ownership if the candidate also built it. The handoff outcome is strong but the subject is fuzzy.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the clearest 'who uses it / what changed' bullet on the page (a real team uses it, real engineers maintain it), and it is weakened by not knowing what the thing is.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the tool does in a few words (e.g., collects and ranks policy-relevant documents?) and whether the candidate built it or only deployed it.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Replace 'space-topic research tool' with a plain description of its function; use 'Built and deployed' only if accurate.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app, in which GPT-4o mini writes suggestions from scraped recipes found by SentenceBERT vector search in ChromaDB, and internal testers rated 93% of meals satisfactory
bullet_feedback.problem: Ownership and status are unclear: 'Building' (in progress, not shipped) for an app owned by someone else, and it is not stated whether the candidate built it solo or as part of a TerpLabs team. The bullet is mostly a component chain (GPT-4o mini, SentenceBERT, ChromaDB) rather than a design decision.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Next to the shipped Tortuga claim, an unshipped feature with a component list reads as weaker than the other bullets and adds little systems signal for a backend reader.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: candidate's role (sole engineer vs team member) and whether it is live or in testing.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: State the role and status explicitly; consider trimming one of the named components unless it explains a choice. If space is needed for higher-signal content, this is the first bullet to cut.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Writing Java logic that decides how much EC2 capacity Amazon Redshift reserves for operations like patching, setting upper and lower bounds that keep availability high without overspending, and backtesting the policies
bullet_feedback.problem: 'backtesting the policies' leaves ownership ambiguous: it is unclear whether the candidate designed the reservation policies or implemented policies specified by the team.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the top brand on the page; a reader wants to know whether the intern is making the capacity decision or coding someone else's formula.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether the bounds/policies are the candidate's design or the team's.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Use a verb that reflects the actual ownership ('Designing and backtesting...' or 'Implementing the team's ... and backtesting ...'), without adding results.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Reduced end-to-end latency 34% for a pipeline routing 6,000+ scraped research documents to inference by replacing S3 staging hops with Kinesis streams feeding Lambda
bullet_feedback.problem: '6,000+ scraped research documents' has no time unit (total, per day, per run), so the scale is hard to judge; 34% has no absolute baseline.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A backend interviewer will immediately ask 'end-to-end latency from what to what, at what volume' to judge whether Kinesis was warranted.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether 6,000+ is a total corpus or a rate, and the rough before/after latency if known.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add the time unit to the volume; the design choice itself is clear and should stay.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Rebuilt the legacy tool developers use to create test-data workflows as a React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation, and 90% of 30+ surveyed developers preferred it
bullet_feedback.problem: 'the legacy tool developers use' can momentarily parse as 'legacy tool-developers'; the tech list (React, TypeScript, Electron, React Flow, Jest) is long relative to the engineering decision it explains.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor read friction on an otherwise strong 'who used it' bullet.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase to 'the legacy tool that developers use' and consider leaving one or two of the framework names to the Skills section.

page_feedback.problem: The strongest systems evidence (IEX matching engine: 50.9M messages replayed, 1.26M events/sec, B+ tree vs LSM benchmark) sits at the bottom of the page, while most of the experience bullets above it are LLM-application work (Claude skill, Bedrock classifier, VLM prompts, RAG).
page_feedback.why_it_matters: On a skim the candidate can read as an 'AI app builder' rather than the systems-oriented engineer the profile claims; a backend HM may stop before reaching the most differentiated work.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Consider moving Projects above the lower-signal roles (UMIACS, TerpLabs), or trimming one LLM-centric bullet so the systems work appears higher on the page.

page_feedback.problem: The IEX project dates (Jul 2026 – Aug 2026) fully overlap the Capital One internship (Jun – Aug 2026).
page_feedback.why_it_matters: A careful reader may ask whether this was done alongside a full-time internship, which invites a credibility question about a large project in two months.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep if accurate, but be ready to explain; if the work started earlier, use the true start date.

page_feedback.problem: Several role subjects are named by internal or project jargon rather than function ('Claude skill', 'space-topic research tool', 'AI workflow generation').
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Non-engineer screeners and engineers outside LLM tooling cannot restate what was built, which lowers plain-language and skim scores even though the engineering is real.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: For each, add a short plain-English noun phrase naming what the system does and who uses it before the technology.

page_feedback.problem: Skills 'Practices & Tools' line includes low-signal items ('data structures and algorithms', 'Agile', 'Jira').
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Takes space without differentiating; every applicant lists these.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Cut or shorten that line; profiling (perf) and testing frameworks are the useful parts.

keep: Built a C++17 order book and matching engine and replayed 50.9M real IEX exchange messages through it without ever resyncing to the exchange’s book, matching 99,122 of 99,123 fills and 100% of top-of-book prices

Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the engine’s event log and benchmarked them on identical 2M-record workloads: the B+ tree gave 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range summaries for 27% more disk
Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end over the full replay, keeping each price level’s orders in a std::list FIFO inside a std::map and a hash map from order ID to list iterator for O(1) cancels

Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings, and fine-tuning runs only when the grades shift past a threshold
Sparse bolding of one metric per bullet and the overall one-page layout
